steps.title: Prepare culture media and reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare all media and reagents as listed in the Recipes section, keeping the exact final concentrations and volumes.

substeps.instruction: ADFNB medium (M1, 50 mL): 23.25 mL Advanced DMEM/F‑12, 23.25 mL Neurobasal, 1 mL Neurobrew‑21, 0.5 mL N2 supplement, 0.5 mL 2 mM L‑glutamine, 0.5 mL Penicillin/Streptomycin (1×), 50 µL β‑mercaptoethanol (1 M), 1 mL BSA (5 % stock) to give 0.1 % BSA.

Skeletal muscle secondary differentiation medium (M3, 50 mL): 48.4 mL DMEM/F‑12, 0.5 mL N2 supplement, 0.5 mL Insulin‑Transferrin‑Selenium, 0.1 mL Penicillin/Streptomycin (1×), 0.5 mL 2 mM L‑glutamine.

Motor neuron medium (M4, optional, 50 mL): 23.75 mL DMEM/F‑12, 23.75 mL Neurobasal, 1 mL Neurobrew‑21, 0.5 mL N2 supplement, 0.5 mL 2 mM L‑glutamine, 0.5 mL Penicillin/Streptomycin (1×), 5 µL GDNF (100 µg mL⁻¹ stock, 10 ng mL⁻¹ final), 5 µL BDNF (100 µg mL⁻¹ stock, 10 ng mL⁻¹ final).
0.1 % PBT (500 mL): 500 mL PBS + 5 mL Triton X‑100 (0.1 % v/v).
Thaw on ice: Growth‑factor‑reduced (GFR) Matrigel, fibrinogen (24 mg mL⁻¹ in 0.9 % NaCl), thrombin, CaCl₂ (1 M stock).
Store reagents as indicated in the Materials list.

steps.title: Fabricate compartmentalised PDMS microdevices
steps.instruction: Mix, cure, cut, and bond PDMS arrays onto 35 mm dishes using NOA‑73, then sterilise and coat with diluted Matrigel.

substeps.instruction: In a 50 mL Falcon tube, mix 2 g PDMS base with curing agent at a 10:1 ratio by pipetting for 1 min, avoiding bubbles.
Degas the mixture in a 4.7 L vacuum chamber at 800 psi for 20 min.
Cure at 80 °C in an oven for 2 h.
Peel the cured PDMS wafer with blunt forceps, place it microchannel‑side down in a sterile 15 cm² tissue‑culture dish, and cut into 2 × 3 or 3 × 3 arrays with a scalpel.
Apply 0.5 µL UV‑curable polymer NOA‑73 to the bottom of a 35 mm plastic dish, spread evenly with a cell scraper, and mark the orientation.
Partially UV‑cure at 55 J cm⁻² for 10 s in a UV cross‑linker (viscosity increase, still adhesive).
Transfer the PDMS array onto the dish so the long axis follows the NOA‑73 spread direction.
Fully UV‑cure the array at 55 J cm⁻² for 1 min on each side.
UV‑sterilise the assembled device under a UV lamp for 20 min.
Add 1 mL of 1:50 GFR Matrigel in DMEM/F‑12 to the dish, remove air bubbles under a stereomicroscope, and degas the microchannels at 800 psi for 2 h.
Use immediately or seal with parafilm and store at 4 °C for up to two weeks.

steps.title: Coat 96‑well plates with lipidure
steps.instruction: Add lipidure solution to each well of a U‑bottom 96‑well plate and dry overnight.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 0.5 % lipidure (dissolved in 100 % ethanol) to each well of a U‑bottom 96‑well plate.
Leave the plate with lids ajar near the tissue‑culture hood air vents and let it dry overnight.

steps.title: Generate neural spheroids
steps.instruction: Dissociate motor neurons and astrocytes, count, and plate them in lipidure‑coated wells to form spheroids.

substeps.instruction: Dissociate CHR2‑YFP⁺ human PSC‑motor neurons with TrypLE (choose a stage allowing live‑cell sorting) and astrocytes with Accutase (5–20 min incubation) adding DNase‑I to prevent clumping.
Count cells with a hemocytometer.
Plate 15 000 motor neurons and 5 000 astrocytes per well in the lipidure‑coated plate using ADFNB medium (optional: mix 50:50 with motor‑neuron medium).
Spin the plate at 1 200 rpm (≈290 × g) for 2 min.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 48 h. Uniform, round spheroids should be visible.

steps.title: Prepare hydrogel mix for spheroid embedding
steps.instruction: On ice, combine fibrinogen, GFR Matrigel, and CaCl₂ to make a 50:50 hydrogel mixture.

substeps.instruction: Mix 160 µL fibrinogen (24 mg mL⁻¹), 40 µL GFR Matrigel, and 0.5 µL 1 M CaCl₂ in a chilled tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Embed neural spheroids in microdevices
steps.instruction: Transfer spheroids into the outer chambers of the PDMS device, embed in hydrogel, polymerise with thrombin, and add medium.

substeps.instruction: Collect spheroids from the lipidure plate into a 10 cm dish containing 5 mL ADFNB medium; gently pipette up/down to dislodge without breaking spheroids.
Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube, keep 1 mL total volume, remove 950 µL medium, and add 50 µL hydrogel mix (final 100 µL, 50:50 medium:hydrogel).
Place the tube on ice and transfer the spheroid‑hydrogel suspension onto the pre‑cooled 35 mm dish (metal block) containing the PDMS array; keep on the cold block to prevent premature polymerisation.
Aspirate any residual GFR Matrigel from the compartments, then add 500 µL ADFNB medium to the dish edge (avoid entering the array).
Using a fine pipette tip under a sterile hood microscope, place three spheroids into each outer chamber of the array.
Rest the dish at room temperature for 5 min.
Add extra hydrogel mix to each chamber until a meniscus of hydrogel sits above the PDMS (prevents spheroid displacement when thrombin is added).
Quickly apply ~30 µL thrombin to the corners of the array (do not pipette directly into chambers) to convert fibrinogen to fibrin.
Rest 5 min at room temperature.
Add 2 mL ADFNB medium gently to the dish and transfer to the incubator.

steps.title: Plate myogenic progenitors after 24 h
steps.instruction: Embed dissociated myogenic progenitors in hydrogel within the central chambers and switch to differentiation medium after 24 h.

substeps.instruction: 24 h after spheroid seeding, thaw GFR Matrigel, fibrinogen, and thrombin on ice and keep the metal block cold.
Prepare a fresh hydrogel mix (160 µL fibrinogen, 40 µL GFR Matrigel, 0.5 µL 1 M CaCl₂) on ice.
Dissociate PSC‑myogenic progenitors with TrypLE or Accutase, count, and resuspend at 20 000 cells µL⁻¹.
Mix the cell suspension 1:1 with the hydrogel mix so the final cell density is 10 000 cells µL⁻¹; keep on ice.
Add 500 µL skeletal‑muscle growth medium to the edge of the dish (avoid spilling onto the array).
Under the microscope, remove residual medium from the empty central chambers.
Transfer ~1 µL of the progenitor‑hydrogel suspension into each central chamber.
Rest 5 min at room temperature.
Add additional hydrogel to create a meniscus above each central chamber and rest another 5 min.
Apply ~30 µL thrombin to the corners of the array (do not pipette into chambers) to polymerise the hydrogel.
Wait 5 min, then gently add 2 mL skeletal‑muscle cell growth medium to the dish and place in the incubator.
After an additional 24 h, replace the growth medium with skeletal‑muscle secondary differentiation medium (M3) to induce 3‑D myofiber sheet formation.

steps.title: Optional optogenetic entrainment
steps.instruction: Stimulate cultures with blue light and record contractile responses for particle‑image‑velocimetry analysis.

substeps.instruction: Position the LED light source 1 cm beneath the 35 mm dish, set intensity to 100 % and stimulation interval to 500 ms.
Record 5‑s videos at 20 frames s⁻¹ using CellSens software, manually triggering the LED during acquisition.
Export videos as TIFF sequences.
Load sequences into the PIVLab Matlab plug‑in.
Set PIV parameters: algorithm = FTT; Pass 1 – interrogation area 64 px, step 32 px; Pass 2‑4 – interrogation area 32 px.
Calibrate time to 50 ms (20 FPS) using a reference image of known dimensions.
Run analysis (Analysis → Analyze!).
Post‑process: apply an 8‑pixel standard‑deviation filter to all frames.
Export velocity magnitude (m s⁻¹) as ASCII text, draw the central myofiber compartment as area of interest, and multiply values by 1 000 to obtain µm s⁻¹.
Combine multiple recordings by aligning contractile peaks.

steps.title: Immunostaining and imaging
steps.instruction: Fix, block, stain, mount, and image the co‑cultures, then analyse NMJ and axon metrics with IMARIS.

substeps.instruction: Wash cultures with PBS, then fix for 20 min in 4 % paraformaldehyde + 15 % sucrose.
Wash three times with PBS.
Block for 1 h at room temperature in 3 % BSA, 0.1 % Triton‑X‑100, and 10 % DMSO.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution: Titin 1:20, TUBB3 1:500, SV2 1:200, AChR 1:100.
Wash three times with 0.1 % PBT.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with secondary antibodies (1:1 000 in 0.1 % PBT + 10 % DMSO).
Wash three times with PBS.
Add 3–4 drops of Vectashield antifade mounting medium to the dish edge, tilt the dish so the medium flows over the compartments, and gently lower an 18 mm coverslip starting at one side.
Image with a confocal microscope, acquiring a 40 µm Z‑stack at 2 µm intervals.
In IMARIS, create a surface for each fluorescence channel.
Generate a colocalisation channel for SV2 and AChR using the automatic threshold tool.
Create a surface for the colocalisation channel and export object data (number, mean area, volume) to quantify NMJ number and morphology.
Export sum area/volume data from the TUBB3 surface to assess axonal outgrowth.
